discovery: Spherical-aberration correction in electron optics, enabling sub-ångström resolution transmission electron microscopy

nominees.name: Harald Rose
nominees.affiliation: Technische Universität Darmstadt / Universität Ulm, Germany

subfield: Condensed matter and materials physics: electron optics and microscopy
motivation: For fifty years Scherzer's theorem said round electron lenses cannot avoid spherical aberration, which limited electron microscopes to resolutions far above the atomic scale. Rose designed a hexapole corrector. Haider built it into a working instrument, and with Urban in 1997–98 they showed that a corrected transmission electron microscope really improves resolution. Aberration-corrected TEM and STEM are now standard in laboratories around the world. They show single atomic columns, light elements, interfaces, dopants and defects, and give quantitative chemical and bonding information through EELS. In my own field, correctors let us determine the atomic structure and composition of nanometre-sized precipitates in aluminium alloys, and that knowledge feeds directly into industrial alloy design. The same is true for semiconductors, catalysts, oxides and battery materials. This invention is a milestone in experimental physics. It made atomic-scale structure directly visible and has had a large impact on materials science and technology.
